questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are notes. All notes are cards. No cards is a tokens.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are not notes.
II. No notes is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No coins is a notes. Some notes are cards. All cards are tokens.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are tokens.
II. Some tokens are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some coins are notes. All notes are cards. No cards is a tokens.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are cards.
II. Some notes are tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are notes. Some notes are cards. All cards are tokens.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are tokens.
II. No notes is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: P = X = T > R < U.
Conclusions: I. P ≥ U   II. T < U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: V = X < R > S < T.
Conclusions: I. T > R   II. R < X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: W > X < U < R > S.
Conclusions: I. S ≤ R   II. U ≤ R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. V < U   II. V < R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth access savings = pa su vo
growth banking digital = vo mi ni
access banking credit = pa ni to
savings digital credit = su to mi
growth access credit = to vo pa
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: to. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = vo, access = pa, savings = su, banking = ni, digital = mi, credit = to.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 28 km east, turns left and walks 28 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. Net displacement is 21 km east and 28 km north. By Pythagoras, √(21² + 28²) = 35 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of H. D is the daughter of H. G is the father of H. How is D related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. G is a parent of H, and D is H’s daughter. Hence D is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: B is the brother of H. H is the mother of G. F is the father of B and H. How is B related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. B is the brother of G’s mother H. Therefore B is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of G. G is the father of H. E is the son of H. B is the sister of G. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of H, and H is E’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 35. New front rank = 18+3 = 21. Back rank = 55 − 21 + 1 = 35.

questions.stem: In a queue of 36 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 14. New front rank = 19+4 = 23. Back rank = 36 − 23 + 1 = 14.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2800 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6278.79. Recover each cost separately: 2800×100/110 + 2800×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 66 and 99 hours. An outlet empties it in 99 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 66. Net rate = 1/66 + 1/99 − 1/99 = 1/66. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 168 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 76. Still-water speed = 21 km/h. Upstream speed = 21 − 2. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:3. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹259200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 324000. Profit ratio is 108:27. Each ratio unit = ₹2400. Total = 135 × 2400.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹15000 earns ₹2250 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16537.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 15000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 110 litres of pure milk. 22 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 70.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 110 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 15 people is 43 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 59. New total minus old total = (15+1)×(43+1) − 15×43 = 59.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 14 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+14)/(x+14) = 3/2 gives x = 14. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 140 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 11.67. Relative speed = (57.6 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 12 m/s. Time = 140/12.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1900. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.
